local.name: a local server (tools/serve.mjs)
local.countedBy: the server that served the file, which is the only thing that can see a worker's requests

firstPaint.label: the first paint: a page of rows, the count, and the six whole-set queries behind the tiles and the charts

pageOnly.label: returning to the unsorted order after a sort — what a page costs when the engine already holds the row groups

sorted.label: re-sorting the whole file by arrival delay and fetching the first page of that order

filtered.label: one filtered query: arr_delay >= 60, its count, and the whole-set queries again

pages.name: GitHub Pages
pages.countedBy: the browser's own network log, the DuckDB worker's requests included — there is no server of ours in the path

firstPaint.label: the first paint: a page of rows, the count, and the six whole-set queries behind the tiles and the charts

pageOnly.label: returning to the unsorted order after a sort — what a page costs when the engine already holds the row groups

sorted.label: re-sorting the whole file by arrival delay and fetching the first page of that order

filtered.label: one filtered query: arr_delay >= 60, its count, and the whole-set queries again

note: The two hosts differ because GitHub Pages permits caching (cache-control: max-age=600) while the local server sends no-store, so on Pages the browser answers DuckDB's repeat reads of the same byte ranges without going back to the wire. Neither figure is a whole-file download.
